proof_summary: Writing the numerator and denominator as \(N_m,D_m\), the proof derives \(v_p(N_m)=\sum_{i\ge1}\lfloor m/p^i\rfloor^2\) and \(v_p(D_m)=\sum_{i\ge1}\sum_{c\ge1}c\lfloor m/(cp^i)\rfloor\), with termwise bounds also establishing \(D_m\mid N_m\). For \(m=np+k\) with \(k<p\), every relevant quotient by \(p^i\) agrees with that for \(np\), while the extra range terms vanish, so both valuations—and hence their difference, the valuation of the quotient—are unchanged.
